canonical_name: Konig edge-coloring theorem for finite bipartite multigraphs
canonical_statement: For every finite bipartite multigraph, the least number of colors in a proper edge coloring equals the maximum incidence degree, with distinct parallel-edge identities counted separately.

source_selection.citation: Denes Konig, Uber Graphen und ihre Anwendung auf Determinantentheorie und Mengenlehre, Mathematische Annalen 77(4), 1916, 453-465, DOI 10.1007/BF01456961
source_selection.definition_locator: printed pages 453-454 define finite graphs with parallel edges and characterize paarer graphs by a two-part vertex partition
source_selection.theorem_locator: Satz C and proof, printed pages 455-456
source_selection.catalog_transport: Satz C supplies a proper coloring with k colors when every incidence degree is at most k; the catalog equality adds the elementary lower bound at a maximum-degree vertex.
source_selection.review_boundary: The inspected source fixes the theorem family, but repository admission, independent German transcription and translation, correction and errata review, and independent H0 acceptance remain open.

domain_and_universes: At arbitrary universes u and v: Graph Vertex Edge has finite actual vertexSet and edgeSet, even when their ambient carrier types are infinite. Edge identities are independent of vertices and therefore preserve parallel edges.
hypotheses: the actual vertex set is finite
the actual edge set is finite
there exists a Bool-valued side assignment taking different values at the two ends of every link
conclusion: HasChromaticIndex G (maxDegree G vertexFinite): G has a proper edge coloring using Delta colors, and every proper coloring palette has at least Delta colors.

encoding_decisions.multigraph: Mathlib Graph Vertex Edge with embedded actual vertex and edge sets; separate edge identities retain parallel edges
encoding_decisions.loop_policy: IsBipartite requires different Bool sides at every link, so loops are excluded; IsBipartite.noLoops kernel-checks this consequence
encoding_decisions.degree: Set.ncard of G.incidenceSet x; finite actual edgeSet makes this a genuine Nat count, with parallel edges counted separately
encoding_decisions.maximum_degree: Finset.sup of degree over vertexFinite.toFinset; the empty actual vertex set has maximum zero
encoding_decisions.proper_edge_coloring: a function from the subtype of actual edge identities to Fin k which separates every distinct pair incident at any common vertex
encoding_decisions.chromatic_index: the conjunction EdgeColorable G k and forall j, EdgeColorable G j implies k <= j, avoiding an invented minimum operator
encoding_decisions.empty_boundary: edgeColorable_zero_of_edgeSet_eq_empty and hasChromaticIndex_zero_of_edgeSet_eq_empty check that an edgeless graph has the empty coloring into Fin 0 and least palette size zero
encoding_decisions.catalog_equality: the checked ExpandedTarget separates the source upper bound at Delta from the elementary lower-bound conjunct

minimal_import_result: Deleting Graph.Basic makes the multigraph surface unavailable; deleting Data.Set.Card makes Set.ncard unavailable. Each deletion makes the exact module fail.

checked_alternate_encodings.boundary: This only unfolds HasChromaticIndex into the Delta-colorability upper bound and least-palette lower bound; graph domain, bipartiteness, degree, coloring, and binders are unchanged.

excluded_alternate_encodings: a finite SimpleGraph or line-graph coloring without a checked multigraph transport
a finite ambient carrier specialization without a checked equivalence to arbitrary carriers with finite actual graph sets
Satz B regular perfect-matching factorization without a checked reduction to the nonregular Satz C root
an arbitrary edge labeling without the incident-edge properness condition

mutation_tests.method: Lean rejects definitional equality with each mutation, and the checker serializes every explicit expression and rejects any mutation fingerprint equal to the canonical fingerprint.

degenerate_cases: Empty vertex and edge sets, edgeless graphs, isolated vertices, Delta=0, one edge, matchings, stars, paths, even cycles, disconnected graphs, nonregular graphs, empty bipartition sides, and parallel bundles are included when the stated hypotheses hold. Loops are excluded by bipartiteness. No connectedness, nonemptiness, simplicity, or regularity hypothesis is added.
